correctness.rationale: An i-edge divergence has its i-factor in the q_i eigenspace; on this sector L is strictly positive. The product heat resolvent on the other coordinates has mass 1/q_i and distinguished-minus-other differences of fixed sign. Summing absolute gradients in direction i gives 2(q_i-1)/q_i; in direction j the other factors have mass one and the distinguished-minus-other marginal integrates to 1/(q_i+q_j), counted in two layers with q_j-1 neighbors each. Expanding the resolvent at the distinguished vertex gives Q_ee=2alpha_i, so the complementary column sum is 1+A_i-4alpha_i. Symmetry identifies row and column norms. For a<b the cut difference is positive by ab>a+b. Conditioning the resistance difference on the remaining factors gives (b-a) E[1/((a+Z)(b+Z)(a+b+Z))]. At Z=0 the resulting difference bound plus the positive remaining-factor contribution works unless (a,b)=(2,3); there the bound from any third factor c is strictly positive since 1/30-1/(15c) >= 0 and c-1-2/(c+5)>0. Equal-size factors tie by permutation. An independent rational grounded-Laplacian computation (python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_45.py 5) tested 31 representative columns across nine products, including (2,3,4) with exact binary-direction values 14/5 and 28/9. This corroborates rather than replaces the proof.
residual_risks: Only the finite test subset was computed independently; the proof covers the whole stated range, not weighted edges or arbitrary Banach-space projections.

value.rationale: The exact direction scores remove a graph-sized projection computation for a natural heterogeneous family and identify all worst directions for both endpoint norms. In particular, the cycle ordering is not a restatement of the cut ordering: diagonal resistance competes with it, and adding a third factor restores a strict ordering that can fail for two factors. This is an exact canonical-projection invariant, not a minimal-projection theorem.
residual_risks: No claim for intermediate norms or optimization over projections.
